 For Subscribers Long frustrated UCLA fans urge others to believe in Bob Chesney 
 UCLA coach Bob Chesney high-fives young fans after a win over Wisconsin at Rose Bowl on Saturday. (Ronaldo Bolaños / Los Angeles Times) By Jordan Puente p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> UCLA football fans are accustomed to watching the Bruins struggle, so it took some time to believe new coach Bob Chesney really could back up his inspirational messages.
 After a big road win against longtime nemesis Oregon, video posted online showed Chesney delivering a fiery speech to his team in the tunnel before facing the Ducks. He relayed the story of Spanish military commander Hernán Cortes telling his crew to burn boats behind them so that there was no way out but forward. The Bruins, he said, had to burn the boats and fight through the Ducks.
 “His speech before the Oregon game — where he talked about burning boats — that just fires you up,” said Brian Jacobsen, a 1987 UCLA graduate. “It makes me want to run through a wall.”

 For Subscribers What we learned from the — bowl-eligible — Bruins’ win over Wisconsin 
 UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach exceeded the expectation of many against Wisconsin. (Ronaldo Bolanos / Los Angeles Times) By Connor Dullinger p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> The Chesney Train is not stopping any time soon.
 No. 9 UCLA football picked up its sixth win of the season Saturday night at the Rose Bowl, defeating Wisconsin 17-7, making the Bruins bowl eligible and the sole undefeated team in the Big Ten and Southeastern Conference.
 Some penciled in a Bruin loss to the Badgers — who were the leading vote getters outside the top 25 in last week’s Associated Press poll — with starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava ruled out for the rest of the season with a knee injury suffered against Oregon.
 But UCLA’s newest conductor, senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, exceeded expectations against a relentless Wisconsin defense, leading the Bruins to victory in his first FBS start.

 USC and UCLA could benefit as College Football Playoff nears 24-team expansion 
 UCLA football coach Bob Chesney photographed in September and SC football coach Lincoln Riley this year. (Getty Image; Los Angeles Times) By Steve Henson p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> Neither USC nor UCLA has made the College Football Playoff since its inception in 2014. Yet the Trojans finished six of those 12 seasons ranked in the Associated Press top 25, while UCLA finished in the top 25 twice and is currently ranked No. 12.
 Reports that the CFP is nearing a deal to expand the field from 12 to 24 teams in 2027 should be tremendous news for both schools. UCLA (5-0) is surging after its rousing upset over Oregon, and USC (6-1) is ranked No. 19 after beating Washington and Penn State. 
 Arduous tests loom during the second half of the season, however, making the chances of getting the nod from the CFP selection committee a coin flip at best.

 For Subscribers UCLA star Wayne Knight never lost faith in himself amid a long journey to Westwood 
 UCLA running back Wayne Knight breaks a tackle by Wisconsin safety Marvin Burks Jr. at Rose Bowl on Oct. 17. (Ronaldo Bolanos/Los Angeles Times) By Connor Dullinger p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> As the kids of Smyrna, Del., bickered about who got to play the role of 5-foot-7 high school star tailback Wayne Knight during their pickup football games, Knight was blazing a trail under Friday night lights.
 During Knight’s senior season, he ran for 1,406 yards and 30 touchdowns. He dominated state competition with the ardent support of the Smyrna community — a rural town centered around fishing, crabbing and waterfowl, with no more than 15,000 people.
 All of Smyrna shut down when it was game day — supporting William Knight, Wayne’s older brother, who won three consecutive state titles and finished his career as the state’s all-time leading rusher.

 For Subscribers Ty Dieffenbach shines in his first UCLA start as Bruins defeat Wisconsin, improve to 6-0 
 UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach passes during the first half of a 17-7 win over Wisconsin at the Rose Bowl on Saturday. (Ronaldo Bolanos / Los Angeles Times) By Connor Dullinger p]:text-cms-story-body-color-text"> Behind a standout performance from quarterback Ty Dieffenbach in his first UCLA start, the No. 12 Bruins defeated Wisconsin 17-7 at the Rose Bowl on Saturday.
 Dieffenbach orchestrated a six-play, 89-yard drive in the fourth quarter to help seal the win for the Bruins, who clinched bowl eligibility by improving to 6-0 under coach Bob Chesney . UCLA is the only undefeated team in the Big Ten.
 Although UCLA (6-0, 4-0) entered with one of the most potent ground attacks in the nation, the Badgers’ stalwart defense — a unit that ranked No. 15 in total defense and ninth in passing yards allowed heading into the game — held UCLA to just 3.2 yards per carry. Heisman Trophy contender Wayne Knight was limited to just 29 all-purpose yards, though he scored his 12th touchdown of the season.
